+name: Broken Link Checker
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+    paths:
+      - '**.md'
+      - '**.html'
+      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
+      - '.lycheeignore'
+      - 'scripts/check-web-archive.mjs'
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+    paths:
+      - '**.md'
+      - '**.html'
+      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
+      - '.lycheeignore'
+      - 'scripts/check-web-archive.mjs'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+# Least-privilege default; jobs escalate individually when needed.
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
+# any workflow step can configure Git.
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  link-checker:
+    name: Check Links
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    # Typical run: <1min with lychee cache. 10min prevents slow
+    # external hosts or Wayback Machine probes from hanging the workflow.
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-link-checker
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      - name: Prepare reconstructable release history for link checking
+        run: |
+          sed 's|https://…|https://example.com/placeholder|g' CHANGELOG.md \
+            > LYCHEE_CHANGELOG.md
+
+      - name: Check links with lychee
+        id: lychee
+        uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2
+        with:
+          # Check all Markdown and HTML files
+          # Exclude case-studies directory - these are research documents from
+          # external repos with references to files and issues that don't exist
+          # in this repository (similar exclusion pattern as eslint.config.js)
+          args: >-
+            --verbose
+            --no-progress
+            --cache
+            --max-cache-age 1d
+            --max-retries 3
+            --timeout 30
+            --host-concurrency 2
+            --host-request-interval 100ms
+            --user-agent 'formal-ai-link-checker/1.0 (+https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai)'
+            --exclude-path '^CHANGELOG\.md$'
+            --exclude-path docs/case-studies
+            --exclude-path dev/log
+            './**/*.md'
+            './**/*.html'
+          # Don't fail the workflow immediately - we want to check web archive first
+          fail: false
+          # Output file for broken links report (used by check-web-archive.mjs)
+          output: lychee/out.md
+          # Write a job summary
+          jobSummary: true
+        env:
+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Check broken links against Web Archive
+        if: steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0
+        id: webarchive
+        run: node scripts/check-web-archive.mjs
+        env:
+          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md
+
+      - name: Fail if broken links were found
+        if: always() && steps.lychee.outputs.exit_code != 0
+        run: |
+          echo "::error::Broken live links were detected."
+          echo ""
+          echo "What happened:"
+          echo "  lychee found one or more broken links in the *.md and *.html files of this repository."
+          echo "  The Web Archive check above provides replacement URLs when snapshots exist."
+          echo ""
+          echo "How to fix:"
+          echo "  1. Review the 'Check links with lychee' step above for a full list of broken links."
+          echo "  2. For links marked with a '::notice::' annotation above, a Web Archive version exists."
+          echo "     Replace those broken links with the suggested archive.org URL."
+          echo "  3. For links with no archive version, either:"
+          echo "     a. Find an updated URL that points to the same or equivalent content."
+          echo "     b. Remove the link if the content is no longer relevant."
+          echo "     c. Add the URL to .lycheeignore if it is a known false positive."
+          echo ""
+          echo "Report location: lychee/out.md (available as a workflow artifact if configured)."
+          exit 1

@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+name: Security
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  pull_request:
+  schedule:
+    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
+
+# Keep the workflow read-only unless a job explicitly needs an additional scope.
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  codeql:
+    name: CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-codeql-${{ matrix.language }}
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      security-events: write
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        language: [rust, actions]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      - uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
+        with:
+          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
+
+      - uses: github/codeql-action/autobuild@v4
+
+      - uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
+
+  dependency-review:
+    name: Dependency Review
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-dependency-review
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      pull-requests: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      - uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v5
+        with:
+          fail-on-severity: high
+          comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure

+---
+bump: patch
+---
+
+### Fixed
+
+- Split the repeatedly timing-out Intel macOS test suite into complementary
+  core and specification shards without raising its 35-minute budget, and add
+  elapsed-time warnings before either shard reaches the cap (#999).
+- Serialize repository writers across release, desktop, Pages, changelog, and
+  benchmark workflows without cancelling in-flight writes (#999).
+- Remove actionable CI warning debt: use the supported Pages timeout, classify
+  intentional reports as notices, and bring every observed source/data file
+  below its warning threshold (#999).
+- Repair stale Links Notation, relative-meta-logic, and CommonsenseQA references
+  exposed by the new link gate, with host-aware throttling for probe reliability
+  (#999).
+- Restrict Wayback diagnostics to Lychee's actual error section so successful
+  redirects are not reported as broken, and replace an unavailable normal-
+  algorithm reference with live university course material (#999).
+
+### Security
+
+- Add CodeQL, dependency-review, and broken-link/Wayback validation gates from
+  the current language templates (#999).

+# Issue 999 / pull request 1000 evidence and analysis
+
+Collected on 2026-08-11 UTC for [formal-ai issue 999](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/999) and [pull request 1000](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1000). +## Executive conclusion
+
+The latest default-branch pipeline did not contain a failing test. Its Intel macOS test job was killed at the unchanged 35-minute job limit while tests were still passing. This happened twice in the three most recent relevant runs; the last successful macOS job took 28m37s, leaving only 6m23s of margin. Cold compilation and one monolithic test invocation consumed that margin as the suite grew. Splitting only the macOS lane into `core` and `specification` shards removes the critical path without weakening platform coverage or concealing the timeout by raising its budget.
+
+The annotation audit also found four recurring false-warning categories: three intentional closure-cache exemptions, an informational self-hosting dry-run report, a Pages timeout value above the action's accepted maximum, and five files in their size-warning bands. The first two are now notices, Pages uses its real 600,000 ms maximum, and every observed file is below its warning threshold.
+
+The complete template comparison found two missing preventive controls (CodeQL/dependency review and link validation) and a workflow-wide concurrency defect. Mixed read/write workflows could cancel repository writers, while the default GitHub concurrency queue can replace an older pending writer. All material repository writers now share a repository-scoped `queue: max` group; read-only jobs keep branch/ref-specific cancellation. The latest template security and link gates were adapted under the templates' Unlicense terms. The first Dependency Review run then exposed a repository-level prerequisite: alerts were enabled but the Dependency Graph had never been generated. Reapplying GitHub's documented vulnerability-alerts setting enabled both features; the SBOM and dependency-diff APIs now succeed.

+## Root causes, alternatives, and selected solutions
+
+### 1. Intel macOS job cancellation
+
+Evidence: both cancelled jobs have the sole primary annotation `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 35m0s`. The latest log shows continuing successful specification tests until GitHub injected `The operation was canceled`. The last green job was already within 6m23s of the cap, and its monolithic suite used 596.47s after cold build/setup work.
+
+Root cause: accumulated compilation plus a growing, serially scheduled monolithic integration/specification suite on the slower Intel hosted runner. It is a capacity boundary, not a hung test. Raising the timeout would postpone recurrence and contradict the instruction to investigate repeated timeouts. Skipping macOS would create a coverage false negative. Changing runner architecture would alter the platform contract.
+
+Selected solution: keep Ubuntu's full suite unchanged and split macOS into two independently timed matrix lanes:
+
+- `core`: all library, binary, and integration tests except the already focused data/census groups and `specification::`;
+- `specification`: `cargo test --test unit --all-features --verbose specification::`;
+- data integrity, census, and doc tests remain in `core` and are not duplicated;
+- the 35-minute macOS limit remains unchanged;
+- both shards emit elapsed-time telemetry and a warning at 70% of budget, so future growth is diagnosable before another hard cancellation.
+
+Cargo's test-name filter is a supported native partitioning mechanism; see the [Cargo test documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-test.html).
+
+### 2. Mixed read/write workflow cancellation
+
+Evidence: `release.yml`, `desktop-release.yml`, and `external-benchmarks.yml` combined cancellable checks with release, Pages, artifact, changelog, or benchmark writers under workflow-level concurrency. Cancelling a superseded workflow can interrupt an already-active writer. GitHub's default concurrency semantics also retain only one pending run, replacing an older pending writer.
+
+Root cause: cancellation scope was wider than the side-effect boundary. This was a false negative because an interrupted writer could leave partial external state even when a newer run looked healthy.
+
+Selected solution: move concurrency to jobs. Read-only jobs use workflow/ref/lane groups and cancel superseded PR/ref work. All repository-mutating release, changelog, Pages-finalization, desktop-finalization, and external-benchmark jobs share `formal-ai-repository-writes` with `queue: max`. Desktop build/vscode artifact writers use tag/lane-specific queues because their outputs are disjoint; finalization joins the global group.
+
+GitHub now documents `queue: max`, a maximum of 100 queued jobs, incompatibility with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and FIFO-by-wait-start semantics in [Control workflow concurrency](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency). The workflows therefore keep writers idempotent and never combine those options.
+
+### 3. Actionlint's stale concurrency schema
+
+Evidence: current GitHub accepts `concurrency.queue`, but actionlint 1.7.12 still reports `unexpected key \"queue\"`. This is tracked in [actionlint issue 657](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint/issues/657). The prior Rust-template issue incorrectly concluded the feature was unsupported.
+
+Root cause: third-party static schema lag, not invalid workflow syntax.
+
+Selected solution: upgrade 1.7.7 to 1.7.12 and ignore exactly that diagnostic text. All other actionlint diagnostics remain fatal. The upstream Rust-template issue received the same official-doc reproduction and precise workaround.
+
+### 4. Pages timeout warning
+
+Evidence: `actions/deploy-pages@v5` warned that `timeout: 1200000` exceeded its maximum and was clamped to 600,000 ms. Its implementation and [actions/deploy-pages issue 165](https://github.com/actions/deploy-pages/issues/165) confirm the backend/action ceiling.
+
+Root cause: the workflow attempted to outwait a Pages backlog with an unsupported input. It gained no extra wait but generated a warning on every deploy.
+
+Selected solution: explicitly use `600000`, retain a job budget above it, and correct the regression test that previously required a value above the action's maximum. A longer wait would require upstream Pages support, so no local value can implement it.
+
+### 5. Intentional policy results emitted as warnings
+
+Evidence: three closure-driven caches exceeded the ordinary 128-record cap but were explicitly exempt because every record was referenced. The release report also announced a hypothetical self-hosting-ratchet decrease even though report mode does not enforce or fail it.
+
+Root cause: annotation severity did not match control semantics. Expected exemptions and dry-run information were rendered as warning debt.
+
+Selected solution: emit GitHub `notice` annotations and matching `NOTICE`/`notice:` text. Enforced cache-cap and self-hosting failures remain failures in their enforcing modes.
+
+### 6. File-size warnings
+
+Evidence and selected remediation:

+| File | Before | Threshold | After | Treatment |

+| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | 1,996 | 1,500 | 1,424 | Removed comment-only and blank-line bulk while keeping executable YAML and adding the new controls. |
+| `data/seed/multilingual-responses-agentic.lino` | 1,421 | 1,400 | 1,341 | Moved one coherent agentic workspace/tool-result family to a second 81-line registered seed file. |
+| `src/web/worker/formal_ai_worker_20.js` | 1,426 | 1,400 | 1,367 | Removed blank lines only; runtime tokens are unchanged. |
+| `src/intent_formalization.rs` | 907 | 900 | 897 | Compacted redundant documentation without changing behavior. |
+| `src/agentic_coding/general_planner.rs` | 979 | 900 | 893 | Removed blank lines and compacted documentation without changing behavior. |
+
+The new seed file is registered in the production Rust bundle, test-source bundle, `RESPONSE_FILES`, and browser loader. This prevents the superficially easy but incorrect fix of shrinking the file while silently dropping responses from one runtime.
+
+### 7. Missing preventive gates
+
+The Rust, JavaScript, and Python templates all now contain link and security workflows. Formal AI had extensive formatting, linting, secrets, compile, test, coverage, release, desktop, change-detection, file-size, and pipeline-terminal controls, but no equivalent gates.
+
+The imported template condition had its own false negative: it passed when a broken live URL had a Wayback snapshot, even though the checked source still pointed at the dead URL. The local gate always fails a nonzero Lychee result; Wayback is diagnostic evidence and a suggested replacement, not an exemption.
+
+The first local Lychee run exposed 24 previously invisible diagnostics. Five were genuine stale links: three references to the renamed Links Notation repository, one repository under the wrong organization, and the retired CommonsenseQA site. Those now target the current repositories. Two diagnostics came from literal `https://…` examples in reconstructed historical release notes and one from a build-stamped local asset. Because `CHANGELOG.md` is byte-reconstructed from release history, the gate checks a generated mirror in which only that unparseable placeholder is normalized; the original is excluded only while its complete mirror is checked. The build placeholder is narrowly ignored. The remaining 16 were probe false positives: nine Wikipedia requests were throttled, five exact OpenAI pages rejected automation, one authenticated Docker settings page redirected through a login loop, and the AIME host rejected the checker. Per-host concurrency and request spacing fix the Wikipedia burst. Ignore rules name only the exact browser/session-only pages, rather than accepting every 403 or excluding whole useful domains.
+
+Selected solution:
+
+- CodeQL analyzes Rust and GitHub Actions on pushes, PRs, and a weekly schedule;
+- dependency review rejects newly introduced high-severity dependencies on PRs;
+- Lychee checks repository links while excluding archived case studies and this immutable raw evidence directory;
+- known stale documentation links are repaired, while host-aware throttling and narrowly scoped ignores prevent authenticated or automation-blocking pages from creating false positives;
+- a Wayback availability helper validates external archival fallback, matching the template pattern.
+- any broken live link remains fatal whether or not Wayback has a snapshot.
+
+These are established components rather than custom scanners: [GitHub dependency review](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/review-pull-requests/reviewing-dependency-changes-in-a-pull-request), `github/codeql-action`, `actions/dependency-review-action`, and `lycheeverse/lychee-action`.
+
+The first remote Dependency Review execution revealed a separate repository-setting dependency. GitHub returned `Dependency review is not supported on this repository` and pointed to Dependency Graph enablement. The repository was public and Dependabot alerts answered as enabled, but SBOM export returned 404 and GraphQL reported zero manifests. GitHub's official REST schema states that enabling vulnerability alerts also enables the Dependency Graph, so the administrator endpoint `PUT /repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/vulnerability-alerts` was called idempotently. It returned 204; SBOM export then produced a GitHub Dependency Graph document, and `dependency-graph/compare/d00c6168...940fbd05` returned the five new Actions dependencies with empty vulnerability lists. The full job log, annotation, REST response, official enablement documentation, SBOM, and comparison are retained in this archive. Skipping the job would have recreated the false negative that the new gate is intended to close.
+
+### 8. Split-seed language coverage
+
+Evidence: the first full replacement pipeline's lint job passed Clippy, rustdoc, file-size enforcement, cache policy, generated-source checks, i18n catalog validation, and language-change parity. `check-language-test-coverage.mjs` then reported the three changed language-facing files, four changed CI test files, and zero languages covered in added test lines. The same command reproduced locally against `origin/main`.
+
+Root cause: splitting a multilingual response family was correctly classified as language-facing, but the first issue regression only checked line limits. Existing older tests happened to cover one moved intent, while no changed test proved that every moved intent remained present for every language or that all runtime registries loaded the new file. The policy failure was therefore a true positive, even though the worker edit itself removed blank lines only.
+
+Selected solution: strengthen the existing sixth issue regression rather than adding language-name comments or bypassing the policy. It now iterates `formal_ai::language::registered_languages()`, requires direct records for all four moved intents, and checks registration in the production Rust bundle, source-test mirror, and browser loader. This both satisfies the diff-aware guard and catches a real missing-file/missing-locale regression. The guard changed from red to `Language test coverage OK against origin/main: en, ru, hi, zh, es`; the same six focused tests and Clippy pass afterward.
+
+### 9. Correct true positives and non-actionable historical signals
+
+These were inspected and intentionally not hidden:
+
+- Pipeline Status failure annotations after a timed-out job are correct: GitHub reports a timeout as cancellation, so the terminal gate prevents a false-green main run.
+- Run 31427622514's `ENOENT` test failure was a true test failure. It predates the latest commit and the next audited run passed; no current reproduction exists.
+- Historical sccache `You've hit a rate limit` warnings came from GitHub's cache service through `mozilla-actions/sccache-action`, not the repository test logic. They were transient and absent from the latest audited runs. GitHub documents cache service limits in [Actions limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits); the upstream behavior is tracked in [sccache issue 1485](https://github.com/mozilla/sccache/issues/1485). Suppressing all action warnings or disabling the compiler cache would hide real failures and increase the macOS critical path.
+- sccache hit-rate summaries, Codecov-not-configured, and coverage-improvement messages are notices, not warning/error debt.
+
+No unidentified root cause remains, so a speculative debug mode was not added. The only timing-sensitive cause now has default-on CI elapsed telemetry at the shard boundary; this is more actionable than an unused application verbose flag.
+

+## Regression and verification protocol
+
+The minimum regression suite is `tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_999.rs`. Before implementation it failed on the missing sharding/concurrency/gates and oversize workflow assertions (`research/issue-999-regression-before-fix.log`). After implementation it passed all six tests (`research/issue-999-regression-after-fix.log`). The suite ensures:
+
+1. exactly two macOS shards retain the original 35-minute budget and complementary filters;
+2. every material writer has the correct queue scope and no mixed workflow has top-level cancellation;
+3. expected policy outcomes are notices and Pages uses its supported maximum;
+4. CodeQL, dependency review, Lychee, and Wayback gates remain wired;
+5. actionlint is current and only its exact queue-schema false positive is ignored;
+6. every file observed in the warning band remains below its threshold.
+
+Final local verification completed successfully:
+
+- the issue-specific CI/CD suite passed 6/6 and the complete CI/CD unit module passed 183/183;
+- the final self-AST census suite passed 8/8 after regenerating the three source-derived documents;
+- the all-features repository run completed every integration executable and its final 2,667-test target passed 2,664 with 3 intentional ignores and 0 failures; doc tests also passed;
+- all-features Clippy passed with warnings denied, every example compiled, and both normal and docs.rs/no-default-features rustdoc builds passed with warnings denied;
+- formatting, actionlint 1.7.12, ShellCheck, changelog reconstruction, fragment-map tests, and `git diff --check` passed;
+- the split seed's Rust, browser, worker, response-lookup, and data-integrity regressions passed (51/51 browser tests and the focused Rust suites are retained in `research/`);
+- the local live-link gate checked 1,071 links with 0 errors after repairing the discovered stale links and classifying only reproducible probe limitations.
+- the diff-aware language-test-coverage policy passed for all registered locales (`en`, `ru`, `hi`, `zh`, `es`) after the split-response regression was made registry-driven.
+
+Remote workflow results are retained in `github/` and `ci-logs/` and are checked against the pushed head SHA before finalization.
+
+## Solution alternatives rejected
+
+- Increase the macOS timeout: masks linear growth and does not address the repeated pattern.
+- Remove macOS or specification coverage: creates a false negative.
+- Mark Pipeline Status green on cancellation: hides timeout failures.
+- Keep workflow-level concurrency and set `cancel-in-progress: false`: blocks useful supersession of read-only PR checks and still allows default pending replacement.
+- Use only `cancel-in-progress: false` for writers: one pending writer can still be replaced; `queue: max` is required by the issue's no-lost-writer standard.
+- Globally ignore actionlint errors: hides unrelated workflow defects.
+- Keep the 1,200,000 ms Pages value: the action clamps it, so it cannot help.
+- Disable sccache: worsens cold-build time to avoid a transient service annotation.
+- Copy language-template release stacks wholesale: would introduce npm/PyPI publishing paths for products this repository does not ship.

+[{"body":"Fixes #977.

## The mechanism behind the whole issue

> **A job killed by `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub as `cancelled`, not `failure`.**

A run whose only non-success job is `cancelled` inherits the run conclusion `cancelled`, which on the runs list looks exactly like "a human pressed cancel" or "a newer push superseded this run". Grey, not red. No failure notification, no entry in the failed-runs filter.

That is why issue #977 describes the pipeline as `cancelled` rather than `failing`. The pipeline *was* broken — it just never said so.

**18 consecutive `CI/CD Pipeline` runs on `main`** concluded `cancelled` between 2026-08-03T18:09 and 2026-08-06T05:13. The visible damage: the newest GitHub Release was **v0.326.1**, while crates.io already served **0.333.0** and git carried tags for eleven versions in between. **Eleven versions were tagged and published with no GitHub Release at all**, and CI stayed grey through all of it.

## Root causes

### RC1 — `Auto Release` hit its 30-minute cap (run `31065367736`)

| Step | Window |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo build --release` | 02:53:54 → 03:02:08 |
| publish to crates.io (0.333.0) | → 03:04:52 |
| clean-install smoke test | 03:04:53 → 03:13:01 |
| free runner disk | → 03:14:16 |
| `docker buildx build --push` | 03:14:21 → **killed 03:22:04**, still at "Compiling fs2 v0.4.3" |

The PR-check `docker-build` job had used the GHA layer cache all along. The four **release** build-push steps had **no cache at all**, so every release recompiled the whole crate inside Docker — twice with Docker Hub enabled. `Create GitHub Release` sits after the Docker push and was never reached.

### RC2 — `E2E Tests (local web app)` hit its 15-minute cap (run `31073507682`)

`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` ran **10 min 36 s**. Every library Chromium needs was already *"the newest version"*; the entire time went to apt fetching **font** packages from `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` at ~30–60 KB/s. That left ~4 minutes for `Running 468 tests using 2 workers`; the job died at test 159/468.

**Compounding defect:** `globalTimeout` was `15 * 60_000` — *exactly* the job cap, which also pays for checkout, `bun install`, the bundle build, `npm ci` and the browser install. The job clock always won, so Playwright never aborted, never exited non-zero, `if: failure()` never fired, and **no report artifact was uploaded** — the one artifact that would have explained the run did not exist.

## Changes

**Errors**
- GHA layer cache (`cache-from`/`cache-to: type=gha`) on **all four** release build-push steps.
- `auto-release` / `manual-release`: `timeout-minutes` 30 → 60.
- `--with-deps` split into an `actions/cache`-backed browser install plus a **bounded, non-fatal** `install-deps` step — in **both** `test-e2e-local` and `test-e2e-pages`. Headless Chromium runs without those fonts, so a slow mirror can no longer end the job.
- `test-e2e-local`: `timeout-minutes` 15 → 40; `workers: 4` under CI (one per vCPU; these specs are I/O-bound).

**False negatives**
- `globalTimeout` 15 → 25 min, now well below the 40-minute job cap, so *Playwright* aborts first, exits non-zero, and leaves a report.
- New terminal **`pipeline-status`** job (`scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh`) that `needs:` **every** other job and runs `if: always()`. Any `failure` is fatal; any `cancelled` is fatal **on `main`** — where `cancel-in-progress` is disabled, so a cancellation can only be a timeout or a manual cancel — and a `::warning::` elsewhere, where a supersede is legitimate.

**Warnings**
- Every action off the deprecated Node 20 runtime: `upload-artifact@v4→v7`, `download-artifact@v4→v8`, `setup-node@v4→v6`, `setup-python@v5→v6`, `checkout@v4→v6`, across all workflows.
- `release.yml` was flagged as approaching its 2000-line ceiling. It is now **1948 lines — below its 1960-line starting point** despite gaining a job: six inline `run:` blocks became scripts, two of which (`configure-dockerhub-publishing.sh`, `invoke-create-github-release.sh`) were *byte-identical duplicates* across `auto-release` and `manual-release`.

Closes #895 (epic #710). CI produced an LCOV file, uploaded it, and never read the numbers — there was no threshold to fail and no way to notice a decrease. This makes the requirement real: coverage is measured, published, and ratcheted.

## What changed

**A non-decreasing ratchet.** `scripts/check-coverage-ratchet.rs` reads the LCOV report, compares each metric against the reviewed floor in `coverage/baseline.json`, and fails the build on a decrease beyond a stated tolerance. Raising a floor is automatic (`--update-baseline`). Lowering one is refused unless `--justification "<reviewed reason>"` is supplied, which is recorded in the baseline as `lowered_reason` — so a decrease reaches review as a sentence in the diff, not two digits changing.

**Published artifacts.** Each denominator emits a human-readable `coverage/summary-<name>.md` (per-metric table, deltas in percentage points, the ten least-covered files) into the run summary, plus a machine-readable `coverage/summary-<name>.json`. Both are uploaded as workflow artifacts with `if: always()`, so a failing run still publishes the numbers that explain the failure.

**Two honest denominators, never averaged.** A Rust percentage and a browser percentage count different things, and one combined number would let a large Rust suite mask an untested website. They are ratcheted separately:

| Denominator | Lines | Functions | Files |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Rust workspace | 86.47% | 44.34% | 408 |
| Browser production JavaScript | 50.48% | 45.54% | 40 |

**Browser coverage, which did not exist before.** `tests/web/` loads the unbundled `src/web/` page scripts and the 24-module worker mirror into a `node:vm` sandbox *under their real repository paths* — which is what makes V8 attribute coverage to the files the browser actually downloads — and boots the worker through its real entry point with the canonical `data/seed/*.lino` corpus behind `fetch`. 48 new tests, run by `npm run test:web` / `npm run coverage:web`.

**The denominator cannot be quietly narrowed.** `coverage/browser-unmeasured.txt` is a committed `path<TAB>reason` inventory of every `src/web/**` file the browser denominator does not measure. A file that is neither measured nor declared fails the build, as does a stale, redundant, or unexplained row. The list can shrink; it cannot grow silently.

**Coverage moved to its own workflow.** `.github/workflows/coverage.yml`, one job per denominator. Nothing in the release graph `needs:` these jobs, so the move changed no ordering; it also returns `release.yml` to 1930 lines, back under the 2000-line ceiling `scripts/check-file-size.rs` documents as debt that must not grow. The triggers, concurrency group, and change-detection gate match release.yml's contract, so a docs-only PR still does not pay for a 25-minute instrumented build.

## Tests

Regression tests for threshold enforcement and baseline updates, as the issue asks:

- **`scripts/check-coverage-ratchet-tests.rs`** — 30 cases run in CI via `rust-script --test scripts/check-coverage-ratchet.rs` in the `lint` job. They pin that a decrease fails, that an improvement only notices, that `--update-baseline` refuses to lower a floor without `--justification`, that an empty denominator is an error rather than a silent 0%, that a missing LCOV file is an error not a pass, that reports are written even when the ratchet breaks, and that the *committed* baseline is valid and carries a real measured floor for both denominators.
- **`tests/unit/ci-cd/workflow_coverage.rs`** — pins the workflow wiring: the gate's own tests run, each denominator is both enforced and published, timeouts and change-gating hold, and (issue #442) no job treats a *skipped* upstream check as a reason to run.

## Verification

Run locally on this branch, all green:

- `cargo llvm-cov --all-features --lcov` then `--only rust` — 86.47% / 44.34%, ratchet held

Note on the Rust floor: it was measured from a full local run of the same command `coverage.yml` uses. A handful of integration cases needing outbound network could not complete in the measuring sandbox, so a green CI run measures at or above this floor rather than below it. This is recorded in the baseline's `evidence` field.

## Docs

`docs/design/coverage-ratchet.md` documents the measurement, the publication format, and the baseline-update policy; `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, and `REQUIREMENTS.md` point at it.

## Status after the merge with `main`

`main`'s PR #966 (epic E69 / issue #916) landed the two **write-side** halves of #909 while this PR was open:

- gemini's `~/.gemini/settings.json` companion file (`security.auth.selectedType`), via `companion "<path>"` seed nodes → `ClientIntegrationCompanionFile` → `write_companion_file`;

This branch had implemented the same two fixes with a *different* data model (a recursive `companions: Vec<Self>`), which is what produced the merge conflict. The conflict is resolved by **adopting `main`'s canonical mechanism** and dropping the duplicate; what remains unique to this PR is the third suggestion in the issue, which `main` does not have: **verifying after configuring**.

## Problem this PR still closes

`--global` reported success and exited 0 without ever re-reading what it wrote, so it could only report what it *intended* to write, never what a client would find. A future drift of the same kind — an export renamed upstream, a settings key moved — silently produces a "configured" client that fails later with an unrelated startup error.

## Fix — the contract as data, checked by reading back

- `headless_require "<kind>=<target>"` declares the startup contract **apart** from the settings that write it, on both `ClientIntegrationGlobalConfig` and `ClientIntegrationCompanionFile` (`env` names an exported variable; `json`/`toml` name `<relative path>:<dotted key>`);
- `auth_refusal "<text>"` entries in each client's `verification` block name the outputs that mean "not configured".

`src/client_integrations/global_verify.rs` consumes that data at two levels:

- **always on** — after every `--global` run, `verify_written_config` re-reads each declared requirement from disk (the tool's own managed block in the shell profile, or a dotted JSON/TOML key) and fails the run when one is missing or empty. No client needed, so it is safe offline and in CI.
- **opt in** — `formal-ai with --global --verify <tool>` runs `probe_headless_start`: it starts the configured client once non-interactively, sourcing the shell profile, and fails when the output matches a seeded auth refusal. A client that is not installed is skipped, not failed.

All user-facing text lives in `data/seed/multilingual-responses-client-config.lino` (en/ru/hi/zh/es) per the R379 doctrine.

./experiments/issue-909-headless-config-gaps.sh   # configures into a throwaway HOME, exits 1 on any missing requirement
```

- `tests/integration/with_formal_ai_headless_global.rs` — 7 tests: the gemini settings file is written / preserved / restored on `--undo`, qwen gets the complete triple inside its own managed block (an operator-owned export outside the block does not count), `--verify` fails on a refusing client and passes on a starting one, `--verify` is rejected without `--global`, and a whole-task sweep runs `--global --all --verify` and asserts **every** registry-declared requirement of **every** client is materialised.

## Review follow-up — `data/seed` conflicts in almost every PR

> we also need to find a way to automatically (using script, that should be saved
> somewhere) reorganize ./data/seed in such a way that, probability of conflicts is
> drastically reduced

The cause is not volume, it is *sequential* sharding. `scripts/close-total.py` filled
`data/seed/closure-generated-NN.lino` in sorted order up to a 1400-line cap, so each
shard's contents depended on the total **size** of every block sorted before it. One
new token rewrote the tail of its own shard and pushed a block into each following
shard. Measured on the pre-fix tree (`198b11cd`, 11 shards), adding a single token:

| new token | shards dirtied |
|---|---|
| `aaa_shard_probe` | **11 / 11** |
| `mmm_shard_probe` | 9 / 11 |
| `sss_shard_probe` | 2 / 11 |
| `zzz_shard_probe` | 1 / 11 |

Two branches each defining one mid-alphabet token therefore overlapped almost
everywhere — hence a conflict in nearly every pull request.

### Fix — content-addressed shards

Each meaning is now placed by a digest of its own slug, `sha256(slug) % SHARD_COUNT`,
over a **fixed** shard count (16) rather than one derived from the corpus size. A
block's file is a function of the block alone, so adding, removing or reparenting a
token touches exactly one shard and leaves the other 15 byte-identical:

| new token | shards dirtied (after) |
|---|---|
| `aaa_shard_probe` | 1 / 16 |
| `mmm_shard_probe` | 1 / 16 |
| `sss_shard_probe` | 1 / 16 |
| `zzz_shard_probe` | 1 / 16 |

Shards land at ~810–990 lines with headroom to the 1500-line data-file limit;
`close-total.py` now **fails** rather than silently overflowing if one exceeds the
budget, telling you to raise `SHARD_COUNT`. Every shard is written even when empty so
the file set stays stable too.

- `experiments/issue-909-seed-shard-conflict-blast-radius.sh` — reproduces the table
  above: asserts the committed shards are idempotent, then adds one token at four
  points in the sort order and fails if any dirties more than one file (or zero, which
  would mean the probe proved nothing).
- `tests/unit/total_closure.rs::generated_closure_shards_are_content_addressed` — CI
  gate pinning every committed meaning to the shard its digest selects, so a future
  refactor cannot quietly restore size-dependent packing. The symptom shows up in
  *other* people's branches, so it would otherwise go unnoticed.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the invariant and when to raise `SHARD_COUNT`.

## Merge with `main`

Resolved: the conflicts were confined to generated artifacts
(`closure-generated-*.lino`, `data/meta/self-ast/`), so they were resolved by
regeneration — `python3 scripts/close-total.py` (`unresolved_distinct: 0`) and
`cargo run --example regenerate_self_ast_census`.

## Reproduction and root cause

Before this change, a non-offline unknown prompt could turn a requested lookup
into fabricated provenance: an `example.org` URL, Unix-epoch timestamp,
prompt-derived digest, and `cache_hit` event were emitted although no transport
or cache read had happened. The same planning-versus-execution ambiguity also
affected provider, ranking, fusion, comparison, and inspection traces.

`external_search_never_fabricates_source_provenance` is the minimum regression:
it exercises the old route and proves an unexecuted lookup now records a policy

## What changed

- Added a single capture boundary that owns the exact response bytes, URL,
  retrieval time, SHA-256, and truthful live/cache state. Live retrieval is
  opt-in; deterministic cache-only replay is the default.
- Made version-2 cache bodies content-addressed and atomically published while
  retaining version-1 compatibility. Replay validates the metadata digest
  shape before path resolution, recomputes SHA-256 from the bytes, and rejects
  corruption or attempted object-path escape.
- Routed contextual HTTP fetch and DuckDuckGo execution through that boundary.
  Provider, rank, and RRF events are emitted only after the provider response
  is captured and parsed; unavailable paths use explicit `*_planned` events.
- Added shared source-research drivers. Captured provider rankings feed RRF,
  captured pages feed `OptionNetwork::observe`, and statement probability/audit
  changes require an explicit classification of the exact capture.
- Made probability and audit provenance constructible from `SourceCapture`,
  preventing callers from assembling an unrelated URL/time/digest tuple.
  Curated registry URLs remain visible as `definition_merge:source_declared`,
  not fake HTTP retrievals.
- Added deterministic Links Notation learning proposals from captured
  observations and derived option state. Promotion to durable knowledge remains
  human-gated; live-versus-cache state is intentionally excluded so replay
  proposes the same lesson.
- Preserved offline curated-project behavior and all supported-language
  surfaces, regenerated seed closure and whole-repository self-AST artifacts,

Fixes #904.

Agent mode answered a repository coding task with a two-step plan whose only steps wrote `.formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino` and `cat`-ed it back. The `verification_command` therefore observed the file the run itself had just written, so it passed *by construction*, and the run ended in a **success** state ("Recorded and verified …") with the working tree untouched. The same plan's `goal` field held the caller's entire system-prompt preamble ("You are an AI issue solver using @link-assistant/agent. General guidelines. …") instead of the objective.

## Root cause

* `compose_general_change_plan` formalized the **whole** raw prompt, so the formalized `source_text` — which becomes `goal` — was the harness preamble. The preamble and the objective cannot be told apart by wording.
* `compose_repository_work_plan` built both steps *and* `verification_command` around `PLAN_PATH`, and `plan_general_change_step` then emitted the `cat` run plus a success-flavoured message.

## Fix

1. **Goal vs. preamble.** The boundary is made explicit rather than guessed: a new seed meaning `request_objective` declares the `request_objective_lead` role with `Slot::Prefix` surfaces in en/ru/hi/zh (`Issue to solve: …`, `Task: …`, `Goal: …`, `задача для решения: …`, `कार्य: …`, `任务：…`, …). `general_planner::objective_text` returns the span after the first **line-anchored** lead, and falls back to the whole request when no lead is present, so plain requests are unaffected.
2. **No self-referential verification.** A repository work item now composes a single `Write` step and names **no** `verification_command`; `links_notation()` omits the field when empty, and the planner no longer plans a `Run` step for that mode.
3. **Planned, not executed.** `GeneralChangePlan` carries a new `terminal_state` (`executed` | `planned_not_executed`). A repository work item ends `planned_not_executed`, and the run's final answer is the new seeded `general_plan_repository_planned` response ("Planned, not executed: …. Nothing the request names was changed. …") instead of `general_plan_repository_complete` — preserving the #843 honesty guarantee.

The meta fixture `data/meta/general-change-plan.lino` records the new field and two new invariants (`no_self_verification`, `planned_not_executed`).

## Reproduction and evidence

```sh
cargo run --example issue_904_repository_work_item
```

`experiments/issue-904/before.txt` (parent commit) reproduces the issue verbatim:

```
  goal "You are an AI issue solver using @link-assistant/agent. …"
  …
  verification_command "cat .formal-ai/general-change-plan.lino"
final answer: Recorded and verified the bounded repository work-item plan for …
```

`experiments/issue-904/after.txt` (this branch):

```
  execution_mode "repository_work_item"
  terminal_state "planned_not_executed"
  goal "https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/904\nImplement the fix in the repository and verify it with tests."
  step 1 … capability "Write"
verification_command: ""
tools used: ["write_file"]
final answer: Planned, not executed: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/904.
```

## Tests

`tests/unit/issue_904.rs` — one test per requirement of the issue, all written against the harness prompt shape from the report:

* `plan_goal_is_the_objective_not_the_caller_preamble`
* `objective_lead_marks_the_boundary_between_preamble_and_objective`
* `repository_work_item_plan_never_verifies_only_its_own_plan_record`
* `repository_work_item_plan_ends_in_planned_not_executed`
* `literal_file_plans_still_execute_and_verify_the_requested_artifact` (no regression for executable plans)
* `repository_work_item_run_reports_planned_not_executed_instead_of_success` (end-to-end replay)

Two existing assertions in `tests/unit/agentic_general_planner.rs` pinned the exact behaviour the issue calls a defect (the `run_command` step and the "complete" response) and were updated to the new contract.

Committed captures regenerated from their generators: the self-AST census (`data/meta/self-ast*`), the self-healing case, the issue-538 Agent CLI session, and the issue-651 self-coding run (re-captured with `examples/self-coding/run.sh` against a real Agent CLI, so `general-change-plan.lino`, `agent-stream.jsonl`, `formal-ai.log` and `session.json` are a fresh end-to-end run, not a hand edit).

Local checks: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features`, `cargo check --examples --all-features`, `check-file-size.rs`, `check-hardcoded-language.rs`, `cargo test --test unit`.

  e2e, and agent CLI e2e while retaining unconditional manual dispatch;
- define `experiments/`, `dev/log/`, and `docs/case-studies/` once and filter
  them before every job-gating output;
- remove the unused `mjs-changed` output;
- retain real release/deployment push conditions and shipping-change behavior;
- preserve a complete incident case study, original run log, requirements,
  research, and revision-pinned audits of the JavaScript, Rust, Python, and C#
  templates.

- Python: https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/40
- C#: https://github.com/link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/40

The reproduction, timeline, root-cause analysis, raw evidence, and alternatives

5. Analysis §7/§10 updated — including the correction that no template ships `.github/dependabot.yml`, so that row was never a real gap — plus changelog fragments and a rewritten PR title/description.

## Working session summary

Both root causes found and fixed; CI is re-running (I'll report when it finishes).

**1. Secrets Scan** — the session transcript committed as evidence contained the workflow's ephemeral `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Redacted every GitHub token literal across *all* committed session logs (`dev/log/issues/781/pulls/803/` had the same leak, not just 808). Verified locally: `check-secrets.sh` → `No secrets found.`

**2. Build macos-x64 / macos-arm64** — upstream bug in `@electron/osx-sign` (`dist/cjs/sign.js:52`):

```js
function validateOptsIgnore (ignore) {
  if (ignore && !(ignore instanceof Array)) { return [ignore] }
}   // no `return ignore` for arrays → undefined
```

Passing an **array** of ignore rules silently discards all of them. That's why both existing mitigations failed at once — our hook passed an array, and electron-builder forwards `mac.signIgnore` as an array too — so codesign ran over the bundled Chrome for Testing framework and died with *"unsealed contents present in the root directory of an embedded framework"*. Confirmed in the log: the hook's entry banner printed but not a single per-file `ignore SKIP/sign` trace line, proving the predicate was never invoked.

Fix: `signingIgnoreRules()` now returns one composed predicate function (`desktop/scripts/adhoc-sign-mac.cjs:61`); `mac.signIgnore` stays as defence in depth. Tests updated plus a new test pinning the upstream quirk — `node --test` 4/4 pass.

Analysis appended to `dev/log/issues/808/pulls/809/analysis.md`; logs in `ci-logs/`. Commit a6f0f040 on PR https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/809. Worth a one-line upstream PR to `electron/osx-sign` adding `return ignore`.

## Working session summary

Found and fixed the real root cause; CI is re-running (I'll report when the macOS builds finish).

**Root cause:** `desktop/scripts/prepare-resources.mjs` copied the Playwright Chromium directory with `fs.cpSync(from, to, { recursive: true })`. Node defaults `verbatimSymlinks: false`, which rewrites every symlink target to an **absolute** path — so the `Google Chrome for Testing Framework.framework` aliases inside the packaged app pointed at `~/.cache/ms-playwright/...`, outside the bundle. Signing itself now succeeded (the earlier ignore-rules fix worked), but `codesign --verify --deep --strict` then failed with `invalid destination for symbolic link in bundle` on both macos-x64 and macos-arm64.

**Changes** (commit `56fa089c`):
- `prepare-resources.mjs`: copy with `verbatimSymlinks: true`.
- `adhoc-sign-mac.test.cjs:70`: the lint job doesn't install `desktop/node_modules`, so `require.resolve('@electron/osx-sign/dist/cjs/sign.js')` threw `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` — that check now skips when the dependency is absent (this was the Lint failure).
- New `desktop/scripts/prepare-resources.test.mjs` regression test, wired into `desktop/package.json` and `.github/workflows/release.yml:463`.
- Evidence and analysis collected in `dev/log/issues/808/pulls/809/`.

Fixes the CI/CD defects behind issue #808 and moves the checks that previously
only ran on `main` into the pull-request stage, so a pull request can no longer
be green while the release it produces is broken.

Fixes #808

## Root causes found (evidence in `dev/log/issues/808/pulls/809/`)

1. **macOS codesign failure on release** — `codesign` refused the bundled Chrome
   for Testing runtime ("unsealed contents present in the root directory of an
   embedded framework"): its framework layout is not versioned. Fixed with
   `mac.signIgnore`, independently of the custom sign hook.
2. **The macOS sign hook produced no output at all** — this was unexplained, so
   the first commit added an unconditional hook-entry banner and routed the
   diagnostics to stderr. On the first pull-request packaging run that
   instrumentation answered it: `app-builder-lib`'s `isSignAllowed()` returns
   early with *"Current build is a part of pull request, code signing will be
   skipped"* whenever `GITHUB_BASE_REF` is set, so the hook is never invoked and
   the app ships without a `CodeResources` envelope. Fixed with
   `CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST` on the ad-hoc step only (no secrets are in play there).
3. **Auto Release blocked by a malformed self-hosting evidence trailer** — now
   validated at pull-request time by a new `evidence-check` job.

## All checks now run at the pull-request stage (issue comment 5020083365)

- Desktop + `.vsix` packaging: the full six-target matrix, macOS signing and the
  artifact smoke tests run on pull requests in **dry-run** mode — every
  publishing step (attest, release upload, `SHA256SUMS`, `finalize`) is skipped.
  Path-filtered so unrelated pull requests do not pay for six runners.
- Docker image build + `verify-formal-ai-dind` runtime contract (`push: false`,
  so it is fork-safe).
- Self-hosting evidence trailers.
- Secrets scan.
- Fresh-merge simulation against the current `main`.

The issue asks for every false positive, false negative, warning and error in CI/CD. The second class — checks that pass without checking — turned out to be the larger one, and it is what was actually blocking releases. Every finding below was reproduced locally before it was fixed; the evidence, timeline and per-finding disposition live in [`dev/log/issues/812/pulls/813/`](dev/log/issues/812/pulls/813/analysis.md).

## The two failures that were actually red

**1. `Auto Release` deadlocked on the self-hosting ratchet.** Two independent root causes:

- *The denominator measured log volume, not authorship.* 599,340 of the 636,240 lines in `v0.300.0..main` — **94.20%** — were captured CI transcripts and lockfiles that this repository *requires* each iteration to commit. Committing the evidence the process demands was itself scored as a regression, so the ratchet could only ever tighten past reach. Artifacts (`*.log`, `*.jsonl`, `*.diff`, `*.patch`, `*.stderr`, `*.stdout`) and lockfiles are now excluded symmetrically from both sides of the ratio, under a new `METRIC_VERSION = 2` so the change starts a fresh comparison epoch instead of silently invalidating recorded history.
- *Enforcement sat where nobody could act on it.* It ran in `record_release`, on `main`, after every contributing commit was already immutable — and it blocked the only mechanism that advances the range. Release-time is now `RatchetPolicy::Report`; enforcement moved to a differential (branch-vs-base) pull-request gate, where the commits can still be amended.

Verified: the exact command that failed in CI now exits 0 — `4.36% (1608/36896 changed lines; 10/119 commits)`.

**2. macOS desktop codesigning.** Not a packaging defect. Run 29752745259 is a `workflow_run` *healing* build of tag `v0.300.0`, which predates the four packaging fixes already merged; the fixed code is proven green in PR run 29746221627 (`considered=1479 skipped=751`). It needs a newer tag, which fix 1 unblocks. Rather than leave this to be re-diagnosed every time, `scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh` now emits a `::notice` when it is packaging a tag that is not the tip of the default branch.

## Checks that never gated

| What | Why it was green |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo clippy` | Ran without `-D warnings`. Every lint in `[lints.clippy]` is `warn`, so the job printed findings and exited 0. The tree is clean today, so adding it promotes existing behaviour rather than introducing failures. |
| `scripts/check-file-size.rs` | Matched directory exclusions as **substrings**, so `.git` hid all of `.github/workflows/**`. Exclusions are now matched per path component; workflows are measured (warn 1500, fail 2000), while third-party workflows quoted under `docs/case-studies/**` stay exempt — reformatting them would destroy the thing they document. |
| workflow definitions and shell scripts | Nothing validated either. A mistyped `needs.<job>` reference fails **open**: the guarded step silently skips under a green check. `actionlint` 1.7.7 (shellcheck-embedded) and `shellcheck --severity=warning` now run in `lint`. |
| desktop library tests | `node --test $(ls … \| grep -v …)` fell back to Node's own discovery whenever the glob stopped matching — a green step running none of the intended tests. The list is built explicitly and an empty list is a hard error. |

## Checks that gated the wrong thing

- `auto-release`/`manual-release` needed only `[lint, test, build]`. A red **`Secrets Scan`** or either E2E suite on `main` still published the crate, the Docker image and the GitHub Release. (`docker-build` is deliberately *not* a gate: it publishes independently and its failure must not block the crate.)
- The desktop `finalize` job ran under `always()`, so a **cancelled** run could `gh release upload --clobber` a partial `SHA256SUMS.txt` over a complete one. Now `!cancelled()`.
- Desktop packaging and VS Code jobs validated a stale merge preview; they now simulate the fresh merge, as `lint`/`test` already did.
- `secretlint` floated to whatever `latest` was at run time. Pinned.
- `$BASE_REF` was unquoted in `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` — a word-split there takes the *skip* branch and reports success without merging.
- `upload-pages-artifact` dropped dotfiles (`include-hidden-files: true`); the screenshot upload was `if: always()` with the default `if-no-files-found: warn`, i.e. green on an empty artifact.

One finding was deliberately **not** "fixed": `scripts/install.sh` is the only script without `pipefail`, because it is the only one running under `#!/usr/bin/env sh`. `pipefail` is not POSIX and aborts dash — the `/bin/sh` a `curl … | sh` install lands in. The rationale is now recorded in the file header so it is not "fixed" later.

## Upstream reports

Three defects reproduce in the templates themselves; all were re-verified against upstream `main` via the API before reporting.

- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#111 — **filed in this iteration**: unquoted `$BASE_REF` in `simulate-fresh-merge.sh`, with a reproduction, a workaround and a suggested fix. (The rust template's copy quotes correctly; python does not ship the script.)
- link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#33 and #35 — already open upstream, so recorded rather than re-filed.

## Verification

- `cargo test --test unit` → **1953 passed, 0 failed** (6 new regression tests)
- `actionlint -shellcheck` over every workflow → exit 0 (type-checking confirmed live by injecting a bogus `needs.secrets-scanX` into a copy and observing the error)
- `shellcheck --severity=warning` over the 17 shipped scripts → exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs` → exit 0

New tests: `releases_do_not_publish_past_a_failing_secrets_scan_or_e2e_suite`, `lint_job_gates_on_workflow_shell_and_clippy_findings`, `check_directory_measures_github_workflows`, `check_directory_does_not_measure_quoted_case_study_workflows`, plus the ratchet exclusion and differential-gate tests.

## Debug output (default off, per the issue)

- `FORMAL_AI_MACOS_SIGN_DEBUG=1` — per-path `[adhoc-sign-mac]` sign decisions; its *absence* from the failing log is what proved the healing-build diagnosis.
- `experiments/self_hosting_ratchet_replay/replay.py` — per-commit attribution, reason and subject for any range, without `rust-script`.

## Second pass: defects found by running the fixed pipeline

Run [29767811026](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29767811026) was the first full run of the repaired pipeline, and it found two more — one introduced by this PR's own first commit.

**`Test (ubuntu-latest)` reported failure with 1953 tests passed and 0 failed.** The suite finished at 18:43:50; `timeout-minutes: 15` killed the job 1.1 seconds later, during teardown. Run 29749095334 on `main` had already done exactly this and was never diagnosed, because GitHub renders a timeout as `cancelled` — indistinguishable from an infrastructure blip. The budget was not padding: checkout plus the two data checks cost ~3m15s before a test runs, the suite takes ~11m, and eight individual agentic/driver tests each exceed 60 s. Recent `main` durations show creep rather than a one-off — 11m02s, 12m27s, 11m49s, 12m57s, **15m16s (cancelled)**, 14m13s. The budget now matches measured cost, and the step emits a `::warning` past 70% of it so the margin cannot be eaten again in silence. Making those eight tests cheaper is separate work with its own regression risk; what is fixed here is the false report.

**The release gates I added would have accepted a timed-out job.** They read `needs.<job>.result != 'failure'`, chosen so a legitimately *skipped* job would not block a release — but the finding above is the proof that a timeout resolves to `'cancelled'`, which is also `!= 'failure'`. Both gates now enumerate the two acceptable results, and the regression test asserts the positive form *and* that the weaker spelling is absent.

**Both fixes were then swept across every job, not just where they had fired.** No `needs.<job>.result != 'failure'` comparison remains in either workflow. Every declared cap was measured against its worst observed run: `coverage` was at **94%** of its 15-minute budget (11m02s → 14m06s across the last eight `main` runs) — one run from the identical false failure — and `lint` at 78% after the new checks accumulated; both were raised, each carrying its measurements inline so the number is auditable rather than arbitrary. `test-e2e-local` (63%) and `docker-build` (23%) have real headroom and were left alone.

That run also independently confirmed the rest: `Self-Hosting Evidence Check` green **on the real PR**, every new lint step green, and [Desktop Release 29767811373](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29767811373) green across all six platform legs including both macOS architectures — the confirmation that current desktop code signs and packages fine, and that run 29752745259 failed only because it was a healing build of the older `v0.300.0` tag.

## The mechanism behind the whole issue

> **A job killed by `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub as `cancelled`, not `failure`.**

A run whose only non-success job is `cancelled` inherits the run conclusion `cancelled`, which on the runs list looks exactly like "a human pressed cancel" or "a newer push superseded this run". Grey, not red. No failure notification, no entry in the failed-runs filter.

That is why issue #977 describes the pipeline as `cancelled` rather than `failing`. The pipeline *was* broken — it just never said so.

**18 consecutive `CI/CD Pipeline` runs on `main`** concluded `cancelled` between 2026-08-03T18:09 and 2026-08-06T05:13. The visible damage: the newest GitHub Release was **v0.326.1**, while crates.io already served **0.333.0** and git carried tags for eleven versions in between. **Eleven versions were tagged and published with no GitHub Release at all**, and CI stayed grey through all of it.

## Root causes

### RC1 — `Auto Release` hit its 30-minute cap (run `31065367736`)

| Step | Window |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo build --release` | 02:53:54 → 03:02:08 |
| publish to crates.io (0.333.0) | → 03:04:52 |
| clean-install smoke test | 03:04:53 → 03:13:01 |
| free runner disk | → 03:14:16 |
| `docker buildx build --push` | 03:14:21 → **killed 03:22:04**, still at "Compiling fs2 v0.4.3" |

The PR-check `docker-build` job had used the GHA layer cache all along. The four **release** build-push steps had **no cache at all**, so every release recompiled the whole crate inside Docker — twice with Docker Hub enabled. `Create GitHub Release` sits after the Docker push and was never reached.

### RC2 — `E2E Tests (local web app)` hit its 15-minute cap (run `31073507682`)

`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` ran **10 min 36 s**. Every library Chromium needs was already *"the newest version"*; the entire time went to apt fetching **font** packages from `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` at ~30–60 KB/s. That left ~4 minutes for `Running 468 tests using 2 workers`; the job died at test 159/468.

**Compounding defect:** `globalTimeout` was `15 * 60_000` — *exactly* the job cap, which also pays for checkout, `bun install`, the bundle build, `npm ci` and the browser install. The job clock always won, so Playwright never aborted, never exited non-zero, `if: failure()` never fired, and **no report artifact was uploaded** — the one artifact that would have explained the run did not exist.

## Changes

**Errors**
- GHA layer cache (`cache-from`/`cache-to: type=gha`) on **all four** release build-push steps.
- `auto-release` / `manual-release`: `timeout-minutes` 30 → 60.
- `--with-deps` split into an `actions/cache`-backed browser install plus a **bounded, non-fatal** `install-deps` step — in **both** `test-e2e-local` and `test-e2e-pages`. Headless Chromium runs without those fonts, so a slow mirror can no longer end the job.
- `test-e2e-local`: `timeout-minutes` 15 → 40; `workers: 4` under CI (one per vCPU; these specs are I/O-bound).

**False negatives**
- `globalTimeout` 15 → 25 min, now well below the 40-minute job cap, so *Playwright* aborts first, exits non-zero, and leaves a report.
- New terminal **`pipeline-status`** job (`scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh`) that `needs:` **every** other job and runs `if: always()`. Any `failure` is fatal; any `cancelled` is fatal **on `main`** — where `cancel-in-progress` is disabled, so a cancellation can only be a timeout or a manual cancel — and a `::warning::` elsewhere, where a supersede is legitimate.

**Warnings**
- Every action off the deprecated Node 20 runtime: `upload-artifact@v4→v7`, `download-artifact@v4→v8`, `setup-node@v4→v6`, `setup-python@v5→v6`, `checkout@v4→v6`, across all workflows.
- `release.yml` was flagged as approaching its 2000-line ceiling. It is now **1948 lines — below its 1960-line starting point** despite gaining a job: six inline `run:` blocks became scripts, two of which (`configure-dockerhub-publishing.sh`, `invoke-create-github-release.sh`) were *byte-identical duplicates* across `auto-release` and `manual-release`.

## Reproducing test

`tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_977.rs` — **all ten assertions fail against the pre-fix tree and pass after** (verified by restoring the original `release.yml` and `playwright.local.config.js` and re-running). It covers: no `--with-deps` in any workflow, browser cache + bounded non-fatal apt step in both e2e jobs, `globalTimeout` < job cap, all four Docker steps cached, release budgets, the gate job's `needs:` covering every job (this caught a job I had missed), the deprecated-action sweep, and the shared-script extraction.

`gate_script_behaves_correctly_for_every_conclusion` runs the gate script for real across success/skipped, cancelled-on-main, cancelled-off-main and failure. `experiments/issue-977-pipeline-status.sh` is the same four cases as a standalone script.

Existing tests in `workflow_release.rs` and `issue_717.rs` were updated to follow the extracted logic into the scripts rather than dropped.

`dev/log/issues/977/pulls/978/` — both full run logs (25 609 and 31 816 lines) with per-step timings, run/annotation dumps, and **`ANALYSIS.md`** with the timeline, per-requirement root cause, prior art considered (`re-actors/alls-green`, `technote-space/workflow-conclusion-action`) and why a 20-line script fits better.

## Upstream reports

The same defects exist in the pipeline templates, so they are filed there with reproducible examples, workarounds and code fixes:

- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#118, link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#123, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#50 — timeout-reported-as-cancelled (all three templates; verified none has an aggregate gate).
- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#119 — uncached release Docker builds. **Verified as rust-only**: the js and python templates have a single, already-cached build step, so this was not reported against them.

Template job-set diff: the rust template has `cargo-lock`, `coverage`, `deploy-docs` and `fresh-merge` as separate jobs. formal-ai already covers all four — fresh-merge via `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh`, Cargo.lock verification in `lint`, and coverage in its own `coverage.yml` (split out under #895 for the same line-limit reason).

## Local verification

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `shellcheck --severity=warning` over all 18 tracked scripts, `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs`, and `cargo test --test unit ci_cd` (**172 passed, 0 failed**) all clean.

## Not addressed, deliberately

- **Recovering the 11 missing GitHub Releases** (v0.326.2 … v0.333.0). The tags and crates.io versions exist; backfilling the Releases is a one-off `gh release create` sweep over historical tags, not a pipeline change, and it rewrites public release history — worth doing, but as its own decision rather than folded into this PR.

- keep current-location questions, Links Notation definitions, British `behaviour` queries, conversation preferences/corrections, associative-memory inspection, and explicit unquoted teaching rules on their intended local routes

- retain failed search/fetch diagnostics instead of rendering an empty successful research result
- add `formal-ai report body --separate-context-links`, which exports and uploads harness, server, and merged context independently with safe filenames and valid link-only Markdown
- preserve the complete reported dialog, requirements mapping, red/green evidence, and a reproducible Formal AI / Agent CLI self-authorship proof

## Root causes and reproducing tests

| Reported family | Root cause and fix | Regression |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local routing | Missing seeded location/control/memory cues and agentic precedence let generic web/document plans capture local turns. Added seed-backed handlers and moved memory inspection before agentic planning. | `tests/unit/issue_989.rs` whole-dialog, location, conversation-control, and memory tests |
| Links Notation definition | The formalization recipe treated the output-format noun as an action. It now requires a seeded formalization verb. | `links_notation_question_falls_through_to_the_symbolic_concept_answer` |
| Web transport failure | Planners checked completed capability state without checking its latest failed observation, while status-less inference scanned arbitrary successful page contents. Planners now terminate with stored diagnostics and prose inference is limited to the leading diagnostic region. | `failed_web_transport_is_reported_as_failure_not_empty_success`, `successful_web_page_with_record_404_is_not_a_transport_failure` |
| Teaching and behaviour rules | The compiler required backtick pairs, and recursive role evidence made generic action words too broad. Added seed-driven unquoted parsing and direct-role matching in Rust/JS, plus British aliases. | `plain_text_trigger_and_answer_compile_and_replay`, `ordinary_file_edits_are_not_mistaken_for_dialog_control`, browser mirror |
| Issue reports | One merged attachment could not produce the three requested links. The CLI now performs three independent gist uploads, suppresses empty fences for link-only attachments, and sanitizes session-derived context filenames. | issue-989 unit tests plus real CLI integrations for three-link reporting and temp-directory path containment in `tests/integration/issue_822_context.rs` |
